title: Seven dead, dozens trapped after hostel collapse in Delhi on September 6
dek: A five-storey residential hostel called Hostel Daze in south-west Delhi collapsed on Sunday, September 6 around 13:30 local time, killing at least seven people and trapping dozens. Authorities confirmed 12 people were hospitalized. Rescue operations were ongoing as of Monday with the exact number of people still trapped unclear. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta cited water accumulation and ongoing basement repair work as contributing factors.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: At least seven people died and 12 were hospitalized in the collapse of a five-storey student hostel near Delhi University's south campus on September 6; the total casualty toll remains unclear as rescue work continues and the exact number of people in the building at the time is unconfirmed.
bottom_line: As of Monday, approximately 80 percent of debris had been cleared but the basement rubble remains to be searched. The final death toll will become clear as rescue work concludes and all bodies are recovered; this number will measure whether the estimated two-to-four dozen occupants cited by eyewitnesses matches official casualty counts.
body:
A five-storey residential hostel called Hostel Daze in the Satya Niketan neighbourhood of south-west Delhi collapsed on Sunday, September 6 around 13:30 local time (08:00 GMT), killing at least seven people and trapping dozens, according to BBC World. Authorities confirmed 12 people were taken to hospital. The exact number of people who were inside the building at the time remains unclear. Eyewitnesses told local media on Sunday that two to four dozen people were present. It is not clear how many people remain under the debris.
A majority of the residents were students attending colleges near Delhi University's south campus, which is a short distance away. Many residents were thought to be in their rooms at the time of the collapse because there were no classes on Sunday. An eyewitness described the collapse as sounding "like the rumble of an earthquake." Four students were rescued who were still breathing. On Sunday, a local legislative assembly member at the scene said that some of the trapped students had been making calls from under the rubble.
By Monday morning, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said approximately 80 percent of the debris had been cleared from the building, with only rubble from the basement remaining. Gupta attributed the collapse to "accumulation of water, combined with ongoing repair work in the basement." A civic official elaborated that seepage from incessant rain may have weakened the structure, and that repair or other work could also have contributed, but "at this stage, however, it is difficult to establish the exact cause."
The building owner has been arrested, and police have registered a case against him and are searching for additional details. Five senior civic officials of the Delhi Municipal Corporation (MCD) have been suspended following the tragedy. The owner of a nearby shop told ANI that the building had been under a 100-year lease and that the leaseholder had undertaken excavation work in the basement to expand the hostel and increase income. Delhi Police said the building had only been 40 or 50 years old.
The collapse raises broader concerns about student housing conditions in the area. Satya Niketan is a densely populated neighbourhood that houses a large student population with many hostels. Many students who come from outside Delhi to attend South Campus colleges are forced to live in cheap private hostels and paying-guest accommodations due to a lack of hostel facilities on campus. A bed in Hostel Daze cost 18,000 rupees (about $190 or £140) per month. Sawai Sharma, a student of Venkateswara College, told BBC News Hindi, "There are 75 students in Sociology Honours class, but only two get a seat in the college hostel. All other students have to live here."
Students report systemic problems with the buildings in the area. Shivam Yadav said most buildings in Satya Niketan are "overloaded" and stated, "The buildings are in a dilapidated condition. No inspections are conducted. There are no rules or guidelines here." College student Ankit Tiwari said conditions at these hostels and paying-guest facilities "are appalling. Students are paying a lot for a very small space which they share with others. There is no proper water or sewage facility here."
The National Students' Union of India called on the government to investigate the cause of the collapse and hold anyone found responsible to account, stating "Negligence with the safety of students and common people will not be tolerated at any cost."
